title: Two Hamzahs in Two Words with differing vowels
titleEn: Two Hamzahs in Two Words with differing vowels
description: When two hamzahs meet across two words their vowels may match (the rules of which were covered in the previous 3 sections) or they may differ. Of the 6 possible combinations when the vowels differ 5 of them occur in the Quran, with the the hamzah maksūrah followed by a hamzah maḍmūmah being the combination that does not occur. Only Imams Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr make takhfif when two hamzahs meet with differing vowels and all of them make the same takhfif in each scenario. Note that takhfif only takes place in the state of waṣl, if a reader was stopping at the end of the first word and continuing from the second word, only taḥqīq can be made.

examples.verse: examples of tashil of second hamzah
examples.note: The first of the two hamzahs will be read clearly (taḥqīq) and the second hamzah with a blend of the long vowel wāw. This example is the only instance of this scenario in the Quran.
